label: tokenization and media-preprocessing non-applicability; unmeasured cache measurement specs
directive_clause: Finish tokenization, tool/schema, prefix/KV, model/artifact and media-preprocessing caches with measured savings.
conclusion: Two of the five directive caches do not describe work that exists on Merc's control plane. Building them would cache nothing useful, add coherence risk, and falsify the checklist. That is an architecture fit finding, not a gap to close with empty scaffolding.

tokenization.what_we_did: Traced every token-adjacent control-plane path. Confirmed the control plane never invokes a model tokenizer. Measured the byte heuristic that stands in for admission/pricing estimates. Stopped without building a cache.
architecture_facts: control/realtime.go:405-410 uses len(upstreamBody) as an UPPER bound on tokens for money reserve and len/4 as a LOWER bound for context admission — not a tokenizer
control/quote.go estimateTokens is a rune/ASCII byte heuristic (4 bytes/token ASCII, 0.9 tokens/rune non-ASCII) used for input-depth and quotes
control/prefix_routing_path.go prefixTokensFromBytes maps 4-byte LE windows to surrogate token ids for routing belief only; comments state forged tokenisation can only cost a miss
Settlement prompt_tokens / completion_tokens come from the engine response, not from a control-plane encode
agent/src/token_cache.rs already exists for the embed lane only (revision-keyed encoding cache inside Embedder); realtime/batch_infer leave encoding to the engine

measured_adjacent_costs.method: go test BenchmarkEstimateTokens* and wall-clock probe on merc/control at commit under measurement; Apple M3 Ultra
measured_adjacent_costs.note: Even a perfect cache of estimateTokens saves sub-microsecond to tens-of-microseconds of pure byte counting that already runs as part of the input scan. There is no repeated model tokenization cost on the control plane to amortise.

tokenization.why_not_built: A control-plane tokenization cache would key empty work. The only production tokenizer on this repo is the agent embed path, which already has TokenizationCache. Inventing a control-plane token-ID cache would force either a tokenizer into merc-control (wrong authority boundary) or a surrogate that is not the engine's tokenizer (wrong identity).

tool_schema.what_it_is: Tenant/profile/policy-scoped prepared-request identity cache for tools/response_format semantic identity. Not a tokenizer.

measured_on_this_host.fraction_of_merc_overhead_claim: ledger cites ~0.3% of merc overhead for this class of optimisation; this run confirms hit path is ~0.4µs and miss path ~12µs on M3 Ultra

prefix_kv.what_is_wired: Scheduler prefers deeper warm prefixes within the same cost class; workers record warmth after serve; optional engine observation can correct stale belief via cached_prompt_tokens when TaskCommit carries it.

server logs: LCP similarity, graphs reused
engine_physical_bound.summary: Confirmed cache hits; ~2618 prefill tokens avoided at p50; prompt_ms warm/cold ~0.045 (~410 ms absolute save at p50); GPU-domain energy warm/cold ~0.06 (~44 J absolute mean save on this workload).

agent/src/pool.rs (warm ModelPool residency with load_ms and rss_delta)
model_artifact.what_is_wired: Disk artifact cache + in-process warm pool so a second job does not re-download or re-map weights under the same governed model id.

measurement_needed.primary: Bound saving = cold_path_ms - warm_path_ms for the same governed model id on the same host, with cold including either missing disk cache (download+verify) or process-cold map/load, and warm a pool hit after warmup.

receipt_shape.model_id: governed id e.g. llama-3.2-1b-instruct-q4 or all-minilm-l6-v2
receipt_shape.cold_load_ms: first load after process start with empty warm pool (disk present vs absent must be stated)

measurement_needed.not_sufficient: Presence of MODELCACHE dir, HF cache hits in logs, or load_ms fields on unrelated benchmarks without a paired cold/warm arm on the same commit.

detail: Agent model pins and pool load_ms instrumentation already exist
Catalogue GGUF / MiniLM artifacts are expected on this machine's HF/model cache from prior canaries
A short env-gated harness can measure cold pool load vs warm hit without a remote GPU

media_preprocessing.what_we_did: Mapped every media-related lane. Confirmed image generation returns 503. Confirmed media_rendering is closed-scene byte-exact rasterisation. Confirmed media_transcode probe is per-job validation, not a reusable intermediate product. Stopped without building a preprocessing cache.
architecture_facts: control/image_generation.go returns 503: no image runtime in service — there is no prompt-to-image preprocessing pipeline

docs/MEDIA_RENDERING_CONTRACT.md and agent/src/render.rs: media_rendering is a closed JSON scene (bg + ≤256 rects) → deterministic P6 PPM; no model, no external assets, no decode/resize/transcode preprocess stage
Existing cell evidence (evidence/perf/runtime-benchmarks/candle-metal-rendering-r1.json, UNBOUND) shows 64x64 closed-scene render wall ~27.6µs — the entire job, not a preprocess stage
media_transcode: agent ffprobe validates input geometry then ffmpeg encodes with a fixed template; probe is validation of the job input, not a product later stages re-consume across jobs

batch exact-reuse is currently kill-switched (batchExactReuseEnabled=false) and identity is batch_infer-only; that is a full-result reuse wiring fact, not a reason to invent a preprocessing cache. When reuse is re-enabled for byte-exact media, the correct cache is exact full-result identity, not intermediate preprocess state

measured_adjacent_costs.method: python scene parse + rasterize upper bound on same host; real rust path is faster (see candle-metal-rendering-r1 slowest_wall_seconds ≈ 2.76e-5 for 64x64)
measured_adjacent_costs.note: Parse/validate is microseconds; rasterize dominates and is already the billable unit (pixels). Caching 'preprocessing' without caching the PPM is solving a non-cost. Caching the PPM is exact-result reuse.

media_preprocessing.why_not_built: No repeated independent preprocessing work exists to amortise. Image gen is absent. Scene parse is trivial. Transcode probe is per-input validation. Exact full-result reuse is the correct work-elimination shape for deterministic media, not a second cache tier.

directive_fit.verdict: The five-cache list partially describes a different kind of system — a monolithic inference gateway that owns tokenization, tool schema compilation, media preprocess, model weights, and engine KV in one process.
fits_merc: prefix/KV routing belief + engine observation (wired; engine TTFT unbound)
model/artifact disk+pool residency (wired; cold/warm bound unbound)
does_not_fit_merc: control-plane tokenization cache — Merc deliberately does not tokenize on the control plane; the engine owns the tokenizer authority used at settlement
media preprocessing cache — Merc has no image-gen preprocess lane; deterministic media is full-artifact work already covered by the exact-reuse design shape
directive_fit.honest_reading: Treat tokenization and media-preprocessing as directive clauses that do not apply to this architecture. Keep measuring the three that do exist. Do not tick the missing boxes with empty caches.
